ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances fix the deviation at 1.90 km: actual 14.6 km minus recommended 12.7 km. That is well over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so this is not a within-tolerance reroute and the driver cannot reach the no-refund rows for a short deviation (rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24). The trip record also timestamps the deviation and rejoin, so the record establishes both the fact and the size of the deviation without any inference.

The driver's device trace measures only 12.318 km over 53 fixes, and the temptation is to say the route was short. POL-RD-22 forecloses that: the trace shows which route was taken and when, but is not used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The recorded 14.6 km and 12.7 km govern, and the 1.90 km deviation stands on those figures.

The LTA record for the recommended route itself — Ayer Rajah Expressway, towards City, from Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct, overlapping the trip window — is advisory type NONE, with speed bands 4 to 6 and the message that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded. POL-RD-23 holds that a reroute is traffic-justified only where the traffic data for the recommended route shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and expressly that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's 'AYE jam already' is therefore bare assertion, and the rider's own account on file — that the AYE looked clear past the slip road — is what the data supports.

The only advisory of an admissible type in the record is the lane-1 roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah. Pasir Panjang Road and Telok Blangah Road are roads on the route the driver actually took, not on the recommended route, which the trip record lists as Clementi Avenue 2, Ayer Rajah Expressway, Keppel Road and Wallich Street. POL-RD-23 requires an advisory that intersects the recommended route; a closure on the road chosen instead cannot excuse leaving the AYE, and the derived read of that artifact itself leaves intersections with the route undetermined rather than shown.

The chat log shows the driver asked 'AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?' and the rider answered 'ok'. That satisfies at most the informed-and-agreed limb of POL-RD-24 row (a), which also requires the reroute to have been traffic-justified; the LTA record for the AYE shows no congestion, incident or closure. Row (a) is therefore closed to the driver, and an 'ok' given on the driver's own unverified premise of a jam cannot convert an unjustified deviation into a no-refund one under POL-RD-21, which licenses a reroute only in response to real-time traffic, a road closure or congestion.

On the applicable row — row (d) of POL-RD-24, not traffic-justified and deviation over 1 km — the rider is owed the excess distance fare in full: deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge. That is 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.37 SGD, which is precisely the figure the fare ledger carries both as the excess distance fare and as the amount already refunded to the rider. The driver's recovery claim asks for a figure the matrix says belongs to the rider.

The 1.37 SGD was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings on 19 Aug 2026 at 01:56:34, and the ledger records the payment as partially refunded with 1.37 SGD refund-issued. The driver filed this dispute to claw that sum back. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, and it never means 'restore a charge'. The rider-favourable, record-consistent outcome is therefore that the driver's claim fails and the state as it now stands — the refund with the rider — is preserved, with no amount moved.

Nothing here needs a human reviewer to fill a gap. Every fact POL-RD-24 turns on is carried by an artifact the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at full weight — the trip record carries the distances and the route, the fare ledger the rate and the refund, the chat log the notice, and the LTA advisories the traffic — so the open-question route to escalation under POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. With the contested amount at 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, the ruling is final at any confidence, and the driver cannot move this to human review to undo a refund the record supports.

The deviation on this trip is 1.90 km, measured the way POL-RD-22 requires: platform-recorded actual distance 14.6 km minus platform-recorded optimal distance 12.7 km (trip_record.derived.v7.deviation). The GPS trace's own 12.318 km is not used to re-measure it, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length. 1.90 km is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so this is a deviation case and not a tolerance case.

The driver informed the rider before the deviation and gave a brief reason. MSG-05006-003 was sent in-app at 18:01:46 - 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?' - and the platform's own route_deviation_detected event is timed at 18:05:06, so the notice preceded the deviation itself; a brief reason is all POL-RD-21 asks for.

The rider acknowledged the notice: she read it at 18:02:06 and answered 'ok' at 18:02:11, and both messages sit inside the trip window (trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip). Under POL-RD-21 the chat log's acknowledgment makes this an agreed deviation, not an unexplained detour, and the driver relied on that agreement in making the turn.

The rider's later statement that 'the AYE looked clear to me' does not unmake the agreement she gave in the chat log. POL-RD-21 makes the chat log itself the test of the rider's acknowledgment, and it records her 'ok' before the driver turned onto West Coast Highway; a rider who accepts the road in advance has agreed to the deviation.

POL-RD-23 asks whether traffic data for the recommended segment shows congestion, an incident or a closure at the trip time. The record's data for that segment is EV-ADVIS-05006-01, covering the AYE (towards City) between Clementi Rd and Keppel Viaduct across the trip window, which records speed bands 4-6 throughout, and the driver's own trace records 28-42 km/h on that stretch from 18:02:04 to 18:04:34. The advisory's type code is NONE, which the driver does not dispute, but the recorded bands and the trace show the corridor was not running free when the driver reported the jam to the rider and rerouted, which is the real-time traffic POL-RD-21 permits a driver to reroute in response to.

On that record the case falls in POL-RD-24 row (a): the deviation is over 1 km, the rider was informed and agreed, and the reroute was made in response to the traffic the corridor was carrying. Row (a) carries no refund, so the 1.37 SGD taken from the driver's earnings on 19 August (fare_adjusted) must be restored to him; read as POL-GEN-03 requires, against the driver's claim and the present state, that is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 1.37, not NO_ACTION.

In the alternative, if the Judge finds POL-RD-23 is not satisfied, the record still leaves open whether EV-ADVIS-05006-02 - a ROADWORK, a closure-kind condition under POL-RD-23, valid across the whole trip window - intersects the recommended route; the artifact itself records that question as undetermined for the Judge. Where the fact POL-RD-24 row (a) turns on cannot be established on the record, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human reviewer rather than finalising a charge against the driver, and under POL-GEN-03 the 1.37 SGD is held rather than refunded while that review runs.

ruling.explanation:
This is a route-deviation dispute about 1.37 SGD, and it is decided on the platform's own records, all of which the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at full weight.

What is not in dispute. The recommended route was 12.7 km (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street) and the driver actually covered 14.6 km (via West Coast Highway, Pasir Panjang Road, Telok Blangah Road). Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the recorded actual distance minus the recorded recommended distance: 14.6 - 12.7 = 1.90 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace's own 12.318 km is not used to re-measure the distance, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length. So this is a deviation case, not a within-tolerance one.

The driver did inform the rider, and the rider agreed. MSG-05006-003 was sent in-app at 18:01:46 ('Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?'), the platform's route_deviation_detected event is timed at 18:05:06, and the rider answered 'ok' at 18:02:11. The notice preceded the deviation and gave a brief reason, and the chat log records the rider's acknowledgment, which under POL-RD-21 makes the deviation agreed. The rider's later remark that the AYE looked clear does not unmake the 'ok' she gave in the log before the turn.

But agreement and notice are not enough. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 - no refund - also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and POL-RD-23 allows that only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The LTA record for the recommended segment (AYE towards City, Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct) covers the trip window but is advisory type NONE, with speed bands 4-6 and a message that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded; 28-42 km/h on the corridor is not congestion by the policy's own vocabulary. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, so the driver's report of a jam does not carry row (a). The only closure-kind advisory in the record is the lane-1 roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah - a road on the route the driver chose, not on the recommended route - so it does not satisfy POL-RD-23 either. The drivers' alternative escalation argument fails on the same point: the advisory's intersection with the recommended route is answerable from its road, direction and location against the trip, and the answer is no, so there is no open question under POL-GEN-26 to send to a reviewer.

That leaves row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, refund of the excess distance fare in full. The figure is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD, which is exactly the sum the fare ledger records as the excess distance fare and as the amount refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings on 19 Aug 2026 at 01:56:34 (fare_adjusted).

Because the driver filed this dispute to claw back a refund the rider is owed, the driver's claim fails. Under POL-GEN-03 and the filing frame, the outcome is NO_ACTION - party-relative, the present state stands - and both amounts are null. The 1.37 SGD stays with the rider. The contested value is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so this ruling is final at any confidence, and the agreement requirement, the rider's overall reliability and the driver's history on either profile are context only under POL-GEN-01 and do not decide this trip. No referral clause applies to a route deviation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
